reasons: The claimed status is compliant, and for a compliant finding no redline or comment is expected — the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs and no comment was raised, which is correct.

The cited text supports the rationale: §3(b) (p0014) is a one-way invoicing/supporting-detail obligation on Contractor and confers no right to examine Company records, usage or premises; the only access provision (p0007) runs in our favour, requiring Contractor personnel to obey Company facility and computer-system security policies.

The absence of any audit/inspection/verification right binding the Customer is strictly better than the preferred position (rare, noticed, off-site, Vendor-cost audits), so there is nothing to constrain and flagging a deviation would be over-flagging against our own party's interest.

The failed deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is expected noise here — a frequency cap cannot be located because no audit right exists in the document; it does not indicate an unlimited audit right.

Classifying this as compliant rather than 'missing' is correct under the playbook: the rule is a protective cap on a counterparty right, so the absence of that right creates no gap requiring a clause. The rationale appropriately flags the residual risk that a future Statement of Work could add a records-examination right.
